chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

"There is no man who withholds a dirham that is due, except that Allah will spend two [dirhams] for him in what is not due, and there is no man who withholds a right from his wealth except that Allah, Exalted and Mighty, will make a snake of fire encircle him on the Day of Resurrection."

He said: I said to him, "A man who knows [the ruling], paid the zakat to those not entitled to it for a period. Is he required to pay it a second time to the entitled ones once he knows them?" He said, "Yes."

He said: I said, "And if he did not know its entitled people, so he did not pay it, or he did not know that it was incumbent upon him, and then learned of that?" He said, "He pays it to its entitled people for what has passed."

He said: I said, "If he did not know its entitled people, so he gave it to one who was not entitled to it, and he had sought and exerted himself [in finding the right recipients], and then learned of the fault of what he did?" He said, "He is not required to pay it a second time."

key_terms.أَهْلُهَا: Its entitled recipients (the poor and specific categories)
key_terms.اجْتَهَدَ: He exerted himself (in seeking the correct recipients)
key_terms.طَوَّقَهُ: He encircled him (with a snake of fire)
key_terms.لِمَا مَضَى: For what has passed (the previous periods of obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat to the wrong recipients due to ignorance or sincere effort?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the spiritual and economic consequences of withholding zakat, linking stinginess to divine compensation through doubled expenditure in vain pursuits. It further clarifies the jurisprudence of *khata'* (error) in distribution, distinguishing between negligent payment to unworthy recipients, which requires re-payment, and sincere efforts that later prove mistaken, which are accepted. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) and the validity of single payment when the giver acts in good faith despite factual error.
